answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a ship paying to dock at a wharf. One operator spawning a hundred raven-dark sockpuppets must lock a hundred deposits, so the cost scales with the attack. On the horizon, proven misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the identity, so honest agents keep their stake while Sybils bleed capital with every fake they mint.
